title: Scripting a JavaScript App in Hazel
question: How does Messed Up Dress Up use hazeljs for its scripts, and how could another JavaScript developer do the same in their own program? Matthew, 2026-11-06, for the meeting with Cyrus on 2026-11-11 (^report(42), item 5; ^ticket(697)). First readers in mind: a group in Cambridge, known to Cyrus, who simulate Petri nets with JavaScript tools of their own.
measurements: A worked example, 043/example/petri.mjs: a Petri net (two processes sharing one lock) whose firing rule is a Hazel program of two modules, built with Hazel.runProgram and called once per event. Run three times in Node v22.23.2 on a laptop (13th Gen Intel Core i7-1370P), hazeljs 0.0.4 installed from npm. Each run: the first build, four events by hand, 2,000 random steps (a fixed stream of draws), the same 2,000 calls to the app's own JS handler, a build with a type error, a build with a hole, two rebuilds, and the 2,000 steps again with the program's tail unannotated. Times are performance.now() around each call; medians and 90th percentiles over 2,000 calls, per run. The game's code was read at kids-choice-games 15181ee0 (Messed Up Dress Up 0.0.491).

builds.what: Messed Up Dress Up 0.0.491 (read, not run)

measures.built.ms: Hazel.runProgram's own ms for the first build of the program (analysis, then evaluation to the handler), milliseconds
measures.steps.call_ms: one call of the Hazel handler with a Step event: the arguments converted in, the rule evaluated, the command converted out; milliseconds over 2,000 calls
measures.js_call_ms: one call of the app's own JS handler (a Fire event), milliseconds over 2,000 calls
measures.rebuild_ms: Hazel.runProgram again after a change to one module's text, and again unchanged, measured around the call, milliseconds, one each
measures.unannotated_tail_call_ms: steps.call_ms with the program's tail Rules.on_event instead of (Rules.on_event : (Net, Event) -> Cmd)
